mission.cluster: the Hns computer-use target model: normalization, the fixed resolution ladder, revalidation thresholds and geometric/semantic/accessibility/window matching

adaptation: CommonJS -> ESM. Every one of the donor's twelve exports is re-exported from `index.mjs` unchanged: TARGET_KINDS, normalizeTarget, targetKinds, describeTarget, resolveTarget, revalidate, distance, centerOf, containsPoint, matchesSemantic, matchesAccessibility, matchesWindow. `target.mjs` holds the ported bodies and `contracts.mjs` holds the value shapes; `index.mjs` is the donor's public surface plus three pass-through names (see the next entry). The bodies are otherwise character-for-character the donor's, including its comments and every message string.

Local declaration instead of import, as instructed. The donor opens with `require('./constants.cjs')` and `require('./errors.cjs')`; both siblings are being ported concurrently by another agent into other directories of this tree. To keep this module independently loadable, `contracts.mjs` declares exactly the three values the donor takes from them and nothing more: TARGET_MOVEMENT (`Object.freeze({ stablePx: 3, updatePx: 10 })`, donor constants.cjs line 264), the CODES `TARGET_INVALID` / `TARGET_NOT_FOUND` (donor errors.cjs lines 25-26), and a `ComputerUseError` class with the donor's exact fields — name, code, details, retryable, controllerId, state and toJSON(). `retryable` reproduces the donor's `defaultRetryable()` answer for the two codes reachable from target resolution: both false. No error code that this module never raises was invented.

`index.mjs` additionally re-exports ComputerUseError and CODES (the donor's callers switch on `error.code`, and that type has to cross the module boundary to be catchable) and TARGET_MOVEMENT (the frozen default `revalidate` uses). All three are the local declarations above, re-exported by identity; none adds behaviour. No new public function, option, threshold, default or error path exists anywhere in this module.

`resolveTarget` is still resolver-driven and pure. The donor's contract is kept exactly: a resolver that is missing, is not a function, or throws degrades the ladder to the next rung instead of failing it, and the reason is recorded on the attempt (`error.code` when present, otherwise `error.message`). Nothing here reads a filesystem, a network, a clock, a random source or the environment, and no time or id is injected because the donor's target model has no timestamp or id to inject — `buildResolved` sets `resolvedAt: null` verbatim.

The donor's `coordinateFallback` audit label, the `(no target)` / `(unresolved)` describe fallbacks, the rank/primaryKind derivation and the candidate-list union are all preserved, because they are the donor's own audit trail rather than presentation.
knownDifferences: DEFERRED, not ported: `createWorkspaceGuard` / `planWorkspaceGate` from `app/computer-use/workspace.cjs` (they call `node:fs.statSync` at two call sites). Not imported, not stubbed, not re-implemented. A stub here would have to invent a workspace verdict.
DEFERRED, not ported: `controllers/file.cjs`'s `isProtectedPath` (it lives inside an `fs.watch`-coupled controller, so it has no standalone boundary).

DEFERRED, not ported: `drivers/win32.cjs`'s `resolveVirtualKey` / `composeHotkey` (koffi native bindings and `child_process`; 73 koffi references). MB-008 forbids new OS backends, so the Win32 input driver, the UIA driver, the CDP driver and the screenshot pipeline are all out of scope here.

No module of the donor's world-state, stabilization, recovery, executor, contract, routing or verification layers is included: this module is the target model only. It resolves against whatever `world` and `resolvers` the caller passes and never observes anything itself.

No DOM, accessibility-tree, Win32 or vision access is performed. The `visual` rung has no world fallback by design (the donor returns null without a resolver), and the point rung's synthetic 1x1 descriptor is the donor's own last-resort label, not an observation.

Donor defects and donor rough edges preserved verbatim and pinned by tests rather than repaired. PURE MIGRATION rejects a 'helpful' guard that would change the result for an input the donor accepts, so nothing below was tightened: (1) a semantic target with no text/label/name/placeholder, e.g. `{ semantic: { inside: '#dialog' } }`, describes itself as the literal string `semantic:undefined`; (2) that same target is an unconstrained predicate and matches EVERY element in the world, so the first pool entry is resolved; (3) a candidate-list wrapper re-walks a candidate's kind with no query, `matchAx` hands the undefined query straight to `matchesAccessibility`, and that throws a TypeError on `query.exact` — the throw is swallowed into the attempt's reason, so a query-less rung is a miss only because the predicate refuses it rather than answering it vacuously; (4) an empty `window: {}` / `visual: {}` object survives `compact()` as an empty object and IS accepted as a rung, describing itself as `window:(any)` / `visual:template`; (5) the synthetic point box is anchored at the requested point, so its rounded centre is one pixel down and right of it (the centre of `{x:10,y:20,width:1,height:1}` is `{x:11,y:21}`) while the embedded element keeps the requested point; (6) `window.className` is case-insensitive equality while `window.title` is a substring, so a `pad` query matches the title but not the class; (7) a beyond-tolerance move with no `ref` on either side reports the text intended for a different node (`target moved Npx and is a different node`); (8) `distance()` propagates NaN for a missing coordinate, and `revalidate` then returns `stale` with the literal reason `target moved NaNpx - re-observe before acting`; (9) an explicit `null` threshold is treated as `0` because `Number(null)` is finite, so `{ updatePx: null }` is not the same as omitting the key; (10) only the boolean `true` selects `exact` matching, so `exact: 1` and `exact: 'false'` both mean substring matching; (11) the flat visual trigger list reads `raw.template` while the built object reads `templatePath` / `template_path`, so a bare `template_path` target is refused with the no-rung message, and `page` / `tab` / `tabId` are read into the target but are not rungs at all, so a bare sheet reference is refused too; (12) a truthy non-integer accessibility `index` is silently dropped (`Number.isInteger` guard) and the field is never consulted by `matchesAccessibility` anyway; (13) `buildResolved` prefers `disabled` over `enabled` and `visible` over `offscreen` whenever the field is merely present, even when it is `false`; (14) a lone `name` is on neither the accessibility nor the semantic trigger list, so `{ name: 'Save' }` is refused rather than treated as text; (15) the `automationId` rule bypasses the `same()` helper, so `exact` never reaches it and it stays a case-sensitive equality against `''`.

Some of the above describe donor intent rather than a coding mistake — `{ name: 'Save' }` being a refusal rather than a text search, or `exact` requiring a boolean — but they are recorded in the same list because either way they are behaviour a re-implementation is tempted to 'fix', and fixing them would change a donor verdict. Every one is pinned in the `donor defects` section of `tests/target.test.mjs` (DEFECT 1 .. DEFECT 15).

parity.vectorSource: DS-Hns app/computer-use/target.cjs @ eeb57ca5c2c56bdf2e58c1216c610b4b9fbc973b, exercised as the real CommonJS module against the port over a generated input matrix (9 973 comparisons, 0 mismatches: every normalizeTarget / describeTarget / targetKinds input, every resolveTarget world and resolver shape, every match predicate's node/query cross-product, geometry, and every revalidate pair and threshold set).
vectors: TARGET_KINDS is the frozen seven-rung ladder with ranks 1..7 and the donor's labels, and rank/primaryKind are the best (lowest-rank) rung present
a window is a standalone rung only when no other rung is present; otherwise it is a locator context that does not appear in kinds
a string target is trimmed, refused when blank, and routed to the selector rung or to semantic text by looksLikeSelector
an object with no addressing rung is refused with TARGET_INVALID and the donor's exact message and `received` details
bbox accepts x/y/width/height, left/top and w/h, requires four finite numbers and a positive extent, and refuses in that order
point accepts point / coordinate / coordinates / a bare x+y pair, the bare pair winning because it is applied last
window accepts a string title or a structured reference; handle is carried as a string and a non-object window is refused
the ladder is walked selector -> accessibility -> semantic -> window -> bbox -> visual -> point, and every attempt before the hit is recorded with kind, ok, count and reason
candidates are tried in order and the wrapper target is tried last

a resolver that is absent, is not a function, returns nothing, or throws degrades the ladder to the next rung instead of failing it; a thrown error's code, else its message, becomes the attempt reason
the visual rung is never resolved from world state: without a visual resolver it reports no match
the point rung resolves inside a containing bbox first and otherwise yields a synthetic 1x1 descriptor labelled `synthetic: true`
the selector rung matches element.selector, element.id or element.attributes.id; the accessibility pool is world.ax then world.controls; the general pool is world.controls then world.visibleTargets

matchesAccessibility: substring by default and equality under exact, role accepting role or controlType, controlType accepting only controlType, automationId a case-sensitive equality against '', and undefined/null expectations ignored
matchesSemantic: the joined name/text/value/placeholder/label text is substring-searched for text, label, placeholder and name, while role is a case-insensitive equality
matchesWindow: handle and processId are typed equality, className is case-insensitive equality, title is a case-insensitive substring, falsy query fields assert nothing
containsPoint is inclusive on all four edges and rounds nothing; centerOf rounds .5 up; distance rounds to two decimals
revalidate: no previous -> unknown, no current -> missing, same identity without geometry -> stable, no geometry -> unknown
revalidate movement bands: < 3 stable, 3..10 updated, > 10 stale, with the thresholds read from the caller and falling back to TARGET_MOVEMENT when not finite
revalidate reports a different node as stale before the band comparison when updatePx is exceeded and the refs are absent or unequal
each verdict's exact reason text, and each refusal's exact message, matches the donor string

resolveTarget's attempt log, resolver degradation and candidate ordering
